**Observations from test image:**
- Split soybean stems showing internal tissue
- Pale whitish pith visible inside stems
- Browning/dark discoloration visible at upper portions
- No obvious black specks or linear structures on the surface

This suggests a stem rot disease. The key diagnostic feature appears to be the **white pith** with some internal browning. Let me view reference images for the most likely candidates.

Looking at the references, I can see a key distinction:

- **SDS** shows white pith in split stems
- **BSR** shows brown pith in split stems
- **Phytophthora** shows chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending from soil line upward with brown coloration throughout

My test image shows split stems with predominantly **white pith** with some browning, which is more consistent with SDS. Let me check a couple more references to confirm.

**Charcoal Rot** shows small black specks (microsclerotia) scattered throughout with gray streaking, which I don't see in my test image.

**Fusarium** shows wilting and brown vascular tissue but not the clean white pith split visible in my test image.

The test image most strongly matches **SDS** features: white pith with some internal browning when stem is split lengthwise. Let me check one more reference to be thorough.

**Diaporthe** shows linear rows of black pycnidia (raised black specks in neat lines), which are absent from my test image.

**Final Analysis:**

Comparing all reference images to my test image:

| Disease | Key Feature | Test Image Match |
|---------|------------|------------------|
| **Sudden Death Syndrome** | White pith with browning | ✓ Strong |
| Brown Stem Rot | Brown pith throughout | ✗ (I see white pith) |
| Phytophthora | Chocolate-brown discoloration | ✗ (too light colored) |
| Charcoal Rot | Black specks (microsclerotia) | ✗ (no specks visible) |
| Diaporthe | Linear black pycnidia rows | ✗ (no linear pattern) |
| Fusarium | General brown vascular discoloration | ✗ (white pith present) |

**Decision:** The diagnostic feature is **white pith with some internal browning when stems are split lengthwise**, which is the distinguishing characteristic for **Sudden Death Syndrome (SDS)** according to the knowledge base: "SDS-infected plants have white pith when stems are cut, distinguishing it from brown stem rot which causes brown pith discoloration."
